title: Wilson-loop (holonomy) vs commuting triangle scores for corrupted-relation detection
setting: 30 entities carry hidden random frames drawn from S3, S4 or Z4 (permutation matrices), and observed edges on an Erdos-Renyi graph carry relations T_ij = g_i g_j^-1, with a fraction of edges replaced by random group elements. Each triangle is scored without training from its holonomy H = T_ij T_jk T_ki: the holonomy method uses the full class function tr(H)/d, while the commuting baseline sees only the abelianization (the determinant/sign for S3 and S4, and the full group for Z4). The metric is the AUC for separating triangles containing a corrupted edge from clean triangles; the diagnostics also report one-round recovery of unobserved pairs.

paper.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
paper.claim: Wilson-loop (holonomy) scores flag corrupted triangles at much higher AUC than any commuting (abelian-sector) score, whose AUC is capped by the group's commutator structure.

metric.name: auc
metric.description: ROC AUC of the chosen method's triangle score for detecting triangles that contain at least one corrupted edge (computed on all observed triangles; labels come from the corruption mask, not used in scoring). Diagnostics: auc_holonomy, auc_commuting (both computed on the same draws), recovery_acc (accuracy on unobserved pairs via one round of composition, using holonomy-weighted or abelian-only aggregation), and n_triangles.

factors.name: method
factors.description: commuting: triangle score and composition use only the abelianized edge operators (sign for S3/S4); holonomy: full class-function tr(H)/d score and Wilson-loop-weighted composition.

factors.name: corruption
factors.description: Probability that an observed edge is replaced by a different uniformly random group element.

factors.name: edge_prob
factors.description: Erdos-Renyi edge probability; controls how many triangles (cycles) exist.

factors.name: group
factors.description: Group of the hidden frames; Z4 is an abelian control where the commuting score loses nothing, so the gap should vanish.
